---
title: "Why Claude Code"
---

This site focuses on one tool, Claude Code, for a few reasons that matter
specifically for research work:

- **It works wherever your project lives.** It runs in your terminal, with
  no separate editor required and no need to move your project into a
  special directory.
- **It reads a lot at once.** A long context window matters when you ask it
  to audit a 30-file replication package or revise a 50-page paper.
- **It doesn't pretend to know what it doesn't.** It's relatively
  conservative about reading a file before answering rather than guessing.
- **It treats you as the principal.** Plan mode, todos, and explicit
  permission prompts before risky actions keep you in control.

None of this makes Claude Code the right tool for every job. The rest of
this page places it next to the alternatives.

## How Claude Code compares

| Tool | What it is | When it's the right call |
|---|---|---|
| **Claude Code** | Agent in your terminal that can read/edit files and run code in any folder | Editing papers, auditing replication packages, multi-file refactors, working in Stata/Matlab/Julia |
| **Cursor** | A code editor (VS Code fork) with an LLM built in | If you live in an IDE and want inline completions + chat in the same window |
| **ChatGPT / Claude.ai (web)** | Chat in a browser; can do "code interpreter"-style work in a sandbox | One-off questions; quick scripts where uploading a file is faster than installing anything |
| **GitHub Copilot** | Autocomplete-as-you-type, plus a chat panel | Fast inline suggestions in VS Code or JetBrains; less useful for multi-file work |

A pragmatic split:

- One quick code question, project not open: use Claude.ai or ChatGPT in a
  browser.
- Inline autocomplete while you type: Copilot or Cursor.
- The AI working on a real project of yours — reading several files, making
  coordinated edits, running things, reporting back: Claude Code (or
  Cursor's agent mode, which is similar in spirit).

Two honest caveats: Claude Code is the right default for the econ-research
workflows on this site, not a universal winner; and you don't have to pick
one. Most colleagues end up using two — an agentic tool (Claude Code or
Cursor) and a chat tool (Claude.ai or ChatGPT) for quick questions away
from the keyboard.
